items.stem: Why is an accurate asset inventory a security control, not just a cost tool?

options.text: You cannot patch or protect assets you do not know you have
options.rationale: Correct: unknown assets cannot be patched, monitored or secured.
An inventory records assets; it does not encrypt them.

options.text: An inventory replaces the need for antivirus
options.rationale: Inventory informs defence but does not replace controls.
Tracking helps detect loss but does not prevent theft.

items.explanation: Correct: unknown assets cannot be patched, monitored or secured.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a CMDB accurate over time? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reconcile automated discovery against recorded entries
options.rationale: Correct: reconciliation catches drift between reality and records.

options.text: Assign clear ownership for updating records
options.rationale: Correct: accountable owners keep entries current.

options.text: Record each asset once and never review it
options.rationale: Static records drift out of date quickly.

options.text: Delete assets whenever discovery misses them once
options.rationale: A single missed scan is not proof of disposal.

items.stem: A laptop is retired. What must happen before it leaves the organisation?

options.text: Its storage is securely wiped or destroyed and the record updated
options.rationale: Correct: data destruction and record update close the lifecycle safely.

options.text: It is switched off and put in storage indefinitely
options.rationale: Storing it does not address the data or the record.

options.text: Only the asset tag is removed
options.rationale: Removing the tag leaves the data intact.

options.text: It is sold immediately with data intact
options.rationale: Selling with data intact risks a breach.

items.explanation: Correct: data destruction and record update close the lifecycle safely.
